title: Counting musicians; cabarets and tunks
summary: Allen asks how many musicians worked; Barnes says mostly cabarets and tunks, explains the difference and names the spots.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: You think there'd be a hundred musicians working in now? You think there'd be fifty, or what number one?
Oh, there'd be a hundred conks. The little ones in the papers.
Conks, the piano players and everything.
Yeah.

Well, how many musicians you figure there were in New Orleans at that time? That would be a question. That would be part of the work, but it wouldn't be nearly all of it. You had a hundred guys probably playing in brass bands, too, huh?

Well, the brass band wasn't a brass band was equalized to the string band. That band was splitting. See, if a man played a funeral or prayed or something like that, well, that day, he'd come to that job that night. See, so you couldn't count that. There's two.
Oh, yeah.
One, yeah.

I see. But that's not what I mean. I'm trying to figure out where most of your work would be in those days. See, the average musician, would he be working mostly in the street or mostly picnics or mostly...
Mostly cabarets. Mostly cabarets.
Mostly cabarets.
Yeah. Mostly cabarets. And where would those cabarets be?
In the district? All through that district. Some different spots in town.

Maybe magazines, street, or the pole in the avenue. Some places up there would have spots with music in it. All up on General Arnold, spots up there with music in it. Take back on Perdita Street and all them streets, Franklin, Grave, you know. See what you mean? Yeah, all of them had it all over Ramport Street. Dryads. Most of them places had the same thing. Three or four piece band, maybe just a piano and drum. Maybe just a five piece band. What about the Red Onion? What would they have in that? Well, you probably got that. I don't think I can give you anything on that. You never went to Red Onion? You never went to Red Onion? No, where's that at?
It was on Ramport, I think about 800-700- lies.

Well, I'mma be right with it for the caller no getting on their name to sing that I got away from me. Yeah, that's away from me. I couldn't come up to it. Not with the truth. See, I couldn't come up to it with the truth. I know most of the places I know.
Spanos, you don't remember?
I don't know Spanos. What was that? Well, that is the same thing. That's a tunk. What do they have? What we call it, tunk and cabaret. Cabaret is a higher grade than what the tunk was.
Would they have a full band and Spanos or piano or what?
Yeah, about a three-piece band. Take maybe a trumpet, you know. Piano and drum. Most of them was piano, drum, clarinet, trumpet, something like that.
